blocking.section: Observability principles (aggregates and sharding) / Cardinality and overhead budgets (Overhead per signal)
blocking.issue: The rule for which families count as hot is wrong for the label sets every request touches. Gateway-scoped Policies (in the worked example `cors-default`, `jwt-default`, `ratelimit-global`, `headers-security` and `geo-block-default`) reach every Route. So every request on the Node records into the same `ruralz_filter_duration_seconds{policy, phase}` label sets. In the SM-4 reference scenario, and on any Node dominated by one Route, every request also records into the same `ruralz_http_requests_total{route}` and `ruralz_http_request_duration_seconds{route}` label sets. These are 'other label sets' with one unpadded atomic per value. At 32 P every core bounces the same `_count` and `_sum` cache lines. A float64 `_sum` also needs a compare-and-swap retry loop, because Go has no atomic float add, and that loop degrades under contention. Contention therefore stays in exactly the scenario that the 2 µs, 40-operation Metrics budget and SLO-GW-2 and SLO-GW-3 are measured in. Sharding only listener and enumeration families does not remove it.
blocking.evidence: Observability principles: "Only hot families shard: listener-scoped and enumeration-only families, at most 1,000 counter or gauge series and 64 histogram label sets (target), into S = min(`GOMAXPROCS` at start, 8) shards (target) padded to 64-byte cache lines." and "Other label sets use one unpadded atomic per value." Overhead per signal: "| Metrics | 2 µs or less (target) | 0 (target) | 24 MiB or less (target) |" and "15 metric operations in the SM-4 scenario and 40 for 10 Filters".
blocking.fix: Define hot by reach, not by label kind. Also shard the label sets of Gateway-scoped Policies (bounded by Gateway Policies × Phases) and the label sets of the first N admitted Routes (target) of the Route histogram and counter, or shard every label set of fast-histogram families. Keep histogram `_sum` as an integer count of nanoseconds (or bytes) with `atomic.AddUint64` rather than a float CAS loop. Add these shards to the memory model (for example 2,000 Route histogram label sets × 192 × 8 ≈ 3 MiB at S = 8) and recompute the Metrics and All telemetry rows. Make the M1 contention benchmark run one hot Route with Gateway Policies at 32 P.

blocking.issue: The 32-interval cap cannot hold once blocked body reads and client writes count as excluded intervals. A pass-through copy alternates an upstream read, gateway copy work and a client write. Because copy work stays gateway-added, adjacent intervals never touch and never merge, so each chunk adds about two intervals. Any unary response of more than about 16 chunks (roughly 512 KiB at 32 KiB reads) or any trickling Upstream exceeds 32. Such requests are then 'skipped and counted' and leave `ruralz_http_gateway_duration_seconds`. That biases the SLIs of SLO-GW-2 and SLO-GW-3 toward small bodies, and the `interval_overflow` counter fills on normal traffic. Separately, parallel `aggregate` legs insert intervals from different goroutines into one pooled buffer, and the document does not say how that stays race-free without a lock on the request path.
blocking.evidence: Gateway-added time: "`ruralz_http_gateway_duration_seconds` is wall-clock time minus the union of excluded intervals: client reads and writes, upstream I/O, State Store round trips and declared remote calls (pack 8.7 rule 6)." and "Upstream I/O is time blocked on the Upstream (pooled-connection wait, dial, TLS, awaiting headers, blocked body reads and writes); Filters and copy work during a leg stay gateway-added. Intervals merge on insert, so parallel `aggregate` legs count once; a request keeps at most 32 (target) in a pooled buffer, beyond which it is skipped and counted."
blocking.fix: Replace the interval list with an O(1) accumulator. Keep a per-request excluded-depth counter and a timestamp. Each blocked section increments the depth on entry and decrements it on exit, and time is added to the excluded total only on the 0 to 1 and 1 to 0 transitions. This is an exact union for sequential and parallel legs alike, with atomics per request and no cap. Drop `ruralz_http_gateway_duration_skipped_total`, or keep it only for clock anomalies. If a list is kept, apply it only to parallel composition and use plain sums for sequential sections, since one goroutine's blocked sections never overlap.

blocking.section: Cardinality and overhead budgets (Overhead per signal, metrics memory model)
blocking.issue: The metrics memory model assumes one collection of live heap, but the budget is RSS, and nothing bounds concurrent collections. The OTLP periodic reader and every `/metrics` scraper each materialize about 120 bytes per exported series. At the 125,000-series limit that is about 15 MB per collection. The OTLP reader, an HA pair of Prometheus servers and an ad hoc curl can overlap, and each overlap adds about 15 MB, so memory grows with the number of scrapers. In addition, 'Memory is RSS', yet the arithmetic sums live bytes. With the default GOGC=100 and no GOMEMLIMIT, the heap target is about twice live heap, so about 23 MiB of live metrics state can show as up to about 46 MiB of RSS. The 24 MiB Metrics and 40 MiB All telemetry rows are then unreachable as written.
blocking.evidence: Overhead per signal: "Memory is RSS above the 96 MiB idle budget (target) in [Tech stack and libraries](../engineering/01-tech-stack-and-libraries.md) (OQ-observability-17)." and "Metrics memory, checked by an M1 heap and contention benchmark at 4 P and 32 P, assumes 120 bytes per counter or gauge series and 300 per histogram label set, 64 × S and 192 × S more when sharded, and 120 per exported series in a collection (hypothesis)." and "so Metrics stays near 23 MiB and All telemetry near 36 MiB (hypothesis)". Observability principles: "For OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-16 this document recommends one `/metrics` exporter reading the OTLP aggregates".
blocking.fix: Allow at most one collection in flight per process. Use single-flight so that concurrent scrapes share one encoded result, cached for up to 1 s (target), and so that the OTLP reader either reuses that result or waits. Better still, stream-encode `/metrics` directly from the aggregates into a pooled buffer, so a collection costs a bounded buffer rather than 120 bytes per series. Then state the memory figures as live heap with an explicit RSS factor, or set a documented GOMEMLIMIT or GOGC policy that the M1 benchmark uses, and recompute both rows and OQ-observability-17.

blocking.section: Logging and access logs (Access logs) / Cardinality and overhead budgets
blocking.issue: The access-log queue memory budget contradicts the record size the document allows. 4 MiB for 8,192 records is 512 bytes per record, but `host` and `path` alone may take 256 + 1,024 = 1,280 bytes. Add a `User-Agent` of unspecified length, the names, IDs, the `failure_modes` list and the `ai` object. A burst of long-path requests fills the queue at about 1.5 KiB or more per record, 12 MiB or more in total, three times the row, and that pushes All telemetry past 40 MiB. If pooled records reference request strings instead of copying them, each queued record keeps its request's header block (up to 256 KiB) alive, which is far worse.
blocking.evidence: Access log fields: "| `method`, `host`, `path`, `truncated` | No query string; `host` and `path` cut at 256 and 1,024 bytes (target), flagged in `truncated` |" and "| `user_agent`, `tls_version` | Truncated `User-Agent`; TLS version |". Overhead per signal: "| Access log, logged request | 2 µs or less at p99, `when` included (target) | 8 or fewer (target) | 8,192-record queue, 4 MiB or less (target) |". Access logs: "The request goroutine evaluates `when` and fills a pooled record for a worker to encode; a full queue drops with a counter."
blocking.fix: Bound the queue by bytes as well as records: reserve each record's actual size from a 4 MiB (target) byte budget and drop with `reason="queue_full"` when it is exhausted. Records MUST copy truncated fields into their own pooled buffer and never reference request memory. Give `User-Agent` a length (for example 256 bytes, target), and cap `failure_modes` and the `ai` object. Alternatively, keep a record count and set the memory row to 8,192 × the maximum record size.

blocking.issue: Folding a retiring label set into `_overflow` together with its accumulated value creates phantom increments. When the retiring ceiling is hit, a counter or histogram that has accumulated, say, 10 million requests or 5,000 5xx disappears, and `_overflow` jumps by that amount in one step. `rate()` and `increase()` over `_overflow`, and every `sum(rate(...))` panel over the family, show a spike of events that never happened in that window. The SLO SLIs that sit on per-resource families can fold this way: SLO-GW-4 (`ruralz_plugin_call_overhead_seconds{policy, phase}`) and SLO-AI-1 (`provider`, `model`). The spike therefore feeds burn-rate rules and can page falsely. The claim that SLO SLIs never fold covers only listener and enumeration families.
blocking.evidence: Cardinality budget: "A Node-wide ceiling of 25,000 retiring series (target) caps a Node at 125,000 series: beyond it the oldest retiring sets fold into `_overflow`, values and late records included; per-Revision admission ignores retiring sets, so live folding stays identical on every Node." and "Listener and enumeration families, including SLO SLIs, are admitted first and never fold." SLO definitions: "| SLO-GW-4 | `ruralz_plugin_call_overhead_seconds` bucket `le=\"0.00005\"` / `_count` |".
blocking.fix: When a retiring set folds, end its series: stop exporting it, and let OTLP and Prometheus staleness close it. Send only records that arrive after the fold to `_overflow`, and never transfer accumulated values. Apply the same rule when a Hot Reload moves a live label set beyond an admission limit. Correct 'including SLO SLIs' to name which SLI families can fold, or make SLO-GW-4 and SLO-AI-1 read families that never fold.

blocking.section: Control plane observability / Grafana dashboards and SLOs (Alert rules)
blocking.issue: Page-severity rules built on `increase()` over rare-event counters miss the first event, and the document says the opposite. A counter series that is first created at 1, such as the first failed Rollout since the leader started or the first `RZ-CFG-027` NACK, has no earlier sample, so `increase()` returns 0 and the page never fires. L counters restart on every failover as new series from a different replica, so any failure shortly after a leader change is lost the same way. `RuralzRolloutFailed` (page), the NACK half of `RuralzTampering` (page) and `RuralzAIProviderCredential` all depend on events that are rare by nature.
blocking.evidence: Control plane observability: "L counters restart with a new start time after failover, which `rate()` and `increase()` tolerate, so nothing extra reaches Raft;". Alert rules: "expr: max by (cluster) (increase(ruralz_control_rollouts_total{state=\"failed\"}[15m])) > 0" with "labels: {severity: page}", and "max by (cluster) (increase(ruralz_control_nacks_total{code=\"RZ-CFG-027\"}[1h])) > 0" with "labels: {severity: page}".
blocking.fix: Require every enumeration label set to be created at 0 at process start, and L series at leadership acquisition before the first event: `state` values, `kind` values, `error_class` values and the registry `code` values that alert rules reference. Add a CI test that each alerted series exists at 0 after start and after failover. Alternatively, alert on the gauges that hold these states (for example `ruralz_control_rollout_state_info{state="failed"}` combined with a change) and reserve `increase()` for dashboards. Restate the `rate()` and `increase()` claim with this precondition.

blocking.section: Metrics catalog (Ruralz Gateway metrics, Degraded states)
blocking.issue: The document says it accepts other documents' proposed names, but the catalog leaves out or contradicts three proposals. A CI gate that 'fails on a panel using an unlisted metric', together with O3's fixed `reason` set, then rejects signals that the sibling designs rely on. (1) Traffic management and resilience proposes `ruralz_upstream_probes_skipped_total` and degraded reason `probes_skipped`; neither appears here. (2) Multi-protocol proposes `ruralz_ingress_hold_expiries_total`, which is also missing. (3) Traffic management and resilience lists `ruralz_cache_store_skipped_total` reason `state_store_memory`, while this catalog and the failure-matrix paragraph use `memory`.
blocking.evidence: Ruralz Gateway metrics: "Other documents' proposed names are accepted, renaming [Traffic management and resilience](09-traffic-management-and-resilience.md)'s `ruralz_upstream_endpoint_ejections_total` to `ruralz_upstream_ejections_total`." and "| `ruralz_cache_store_skipped_total` | Counter | stores | `policy`, `reason` | size_limit, buffer_budget, memory |". Traffic management and resilience: "skipped probes count in `ruralz_upstream_probes_skipped_total` and, above 10% for 1 minute, raise degraded reason `probes_skipped` (target), both proposed to Observability" and "`ruralz_cache_store_skipped_total` reasons are `size_limit`, `buffer_budget` and `state_store_memory`." Multi-protocol: "letting `AckWait` redeliver (`ruralz_ingress_hold_expiries_total`, proposed)".
blocking.fix: Add the missing rows: `ruralz_upstream_probes_skipped_total` (Counter, probes, `upstream`, Planned (M1)) and `ruralz_ingress_hold_expiries_total` (Counter, holds, `route`, `protocol`, Planned (M4)). Add `probes_skipped` to Degraded states. Pick one cache skip reason: `state_store_memory` matches the degraded-reason naming. Use it in the table and in the failure-matrix sentence, and record the choice so Traffic management and resilience conforms. Add a CI check that every `ruralz_*` name in docs/architecture appears in this catalog.

non_blocking.suggestion: The two per-Node token buckets are one shared atomic each. Under OQ-observability-4 option (a), a client that sets the sampled flag on every request makes every request run a compare-and-swap on the parent bucket's cache line, which is new request-path contention. Split each bucket across the S stripes at rate/S and burst/S (target), consulted with the request's stripe, as the metric shards are.

'A lock-free per-connection random source' cannot be lock-free when up to 250 HTTP/2 streams of one connection generate IDs concurrently. Use the top-level `math/rand/v2` functions, which draw from the runtime's per-thread ChaCha8 source without locks, or give each source to a stream, and state that the 1 µs and 2-allocation unsampled budget includes ID generation.

non_blocking.section: Observability principles / Grafana dashboards and SLOs (Route detail exemplars)
non_blocking.suggestion: O6 and the Route detail Grafana dashboard promise exemplars, but the Ruralz-owned atomic aggregates have no exemplar storage. A trace ID, value and timestamp cannot be updated atomically, and neither the memory model nor the zero-allocation path accounts for it. Specify one exemplar slot per histogram label set, written only by sampled requests under a seqlock or pointer swap from a pool, and add its bytes to the memory model.

'OTLP across TB-12 MUST use TLS' is immediately followed by 'the Node still exports' over cleartext, so the MUST is not enforced. Either reject a cleartext endpoint (RZ-CFG) until OQ-security-and-identity-29 closes, or word the rule as Security and identity does: TLS when configured, cleartext reported as a degraded state.

`RuralzAIProviderCredential` counts only `ruralz_ai_fallbacks_total{error_class="credential"}`. A credential failure on a single-candidate `AIModel`, or on the last candidate, produces no fallback, because there is no `to`, so the most common setup never alerts. Count credential failures on `ruralz_ai_failed_attempts_total` with an `error_class` label, or add a dedicated counter.

Because a partial success counts as failure and export never drops, a single record the Collector always rejects (too large or malformed) stops audit export for good, and the lag grows without bound. Define what happens then: after N retries (target), park the batch, raise a degraded reason and record an audit event, with an operator command to skip it. Or state that operator action is the only remedy.

non_blocking.section: Cardinality and overhead budgets (Cardinality budget table)
non_blocking.suggestion: The Plugin histograms row reads 1,600, but three Plugin histogram families (`call_duration`, `call_overhead`, `pool_wait`) × 50 Policies × 16 give at least 2,400, and more for Plugins with several Phases. Recompute that row, the 65,600 and 81,600 totals and the memory estimate that depends on them.

SLO-AI-1 mixes units: `ruralz_ai_settlements_total` counts attempts ('Attempts settled with reported usage'), while `ruralz_ai_usage_missing_total` counts requests. With Provider Fallback, a request can add to both. State one unit, preferably attempts, for both counters and the AI/LLM gateway settlement table.

'Streams can pin four disjoint Route name sets for hours' overstates the case. Per Data plane, the closing snapshot ends its streams at once and stays pinned only for the 30 s grace period and the ending bound. So three sets (active plus K = 2 retired) persist for hours, and the fourth persists for seconds. The 25,000 ceiling is still right, but the rationale should match.

The sharded set is capped at 1,000 counter or gauge series, but `ruralz_http_listener_requests_total` alone has up to 10 protocols × 5 status classes × 3 origins = 150 series per listener. Say what happens to hot label sets beyond the cap (unsharded, admitted in listener order) so behavior is deterministic.
